currentContext.expansion: During the year, the Company acquired a controlling stake (48.80% fully diluted) in J. B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals Limited (JBCPL/JB Pharma), completed January 21, 2026, via share purchase agreements with promoter Tau Investment Holdings Pte. Ltd. and certain employees, plus a mandatory open offer under SEBI takeover regulations; the acquisition is expected to strengthen the domestic (IPM) foundation, expand the therapeutic footprint, broaden the international presence (US, Russia, South Africa) and provide entry into the CDMO segment (medicated lozenges). On the core manufacturing network, the Company operates 8 state-of-the-art facilities across India (excluding JB Pharma) — Indrad, Dahej, Bileshwarpura (a dedicated oral oncology unit representing recent expansion into oncology), Baddi, Sikkim (Units I, II and III), Vizag and Pithampur. During the year the Company undertook capacity and infrastructure investments at Baddi (advanced equipment including high-capacity conta blenders), Bileshwarpura (spray-drying technology, wallet packaging for oncology, and small-batch manufacturing areas under development for niche/specialty products), Sikkim (new bottle packing line and IR dryer) and Dahej (dedicated oral powder manufacturing area and new bottle packaging lines). Looking ahead, the Company is planning to expand warehousing infrastructure, undertake further batch-size scale-ups, deploy advanced equipment and continue automation of manufacturing and quality systems, and to build capabilities for small-batch and high-potency products.

risks.risk: Strategic / product-development and patent litigation risk
risks.note: Pharmaceutical product development carries high uncertainty in clinical outcomes and technical complexity; delayed regulatory approvals or pending patent litigation can delay or force abandonment of launches, and an adverse court ruling could bring substantial infringement liabilities and litigation costs. This risk is currently live: the Company is facing litigation on two products, Losartan and Valsartan, in the US.

In Generics (US, Germany) the Company faces price erosion from consolidated buying groups, managed-care organisations and competitive tender bidding by insurers; in Branded Generics (India, Brazil) it faces pricing pressure from drug price controls (NLEM), government generic-promotion initiatives and pure-generic competition.

risks.risk: Product quality and regulatory compliance risk
risks.note: Operating in a highly regulated sector, failure to comply with cGMP and quality regulations at own or third-party/contract manufacturing sites can trigger regulatory warnings, delayed approvals, facility certification withdrawal, product recalls, product liability claims or licence cancellation, adversely impacting brand and reputation.

risks.risk: Supply chain and single-source dependency risk
risks.note: The Company depends on third-party suppliers for sourcing in some markets and, for certain products, has only one supplier listed in its regulatory application; disruption at in-house or third-party manufacturing/API sourcing locations (economic, regulatory, political or quality-related) can impair its ability to produce and ship on time.

risks.risk: Financial risk (currency, interest rate, cross-border tax)
risks.note: Global operations expose the Company to foreign-currency risk on export/import transactions and overseas borrowings, interest-rate risk on variable-rate borrowings, and tax exposure from differing interpretations of cross-border transactions by tax authorities in various jurisdictions, which could increase tax liability including interest and penalties.

A significant portion of revenue in various markets is derived from a limited number of customers; loss of business from, or payment difficulties at, such a customer could impact business performance.

Capital deployed to add manufacturing capacity carries risk of delayed implementation and cost overruns, as well as the possibility of demand slumping by project completion, resulting in underutilised capacity and higher unit manufacturing costs.

The Company continuously pursues inorganic growth opportunities (most recently the JB Pharma acquisition); integrating people, systems and processes involves significant challenges requiring considerable time, resources and effort, and can temporarily disrupt ongoing business and employee/customer relationships.

one-line thesis: Torrent Pharmaceuticals is delivering robust double-digit growth in India and Brazil through strong new launches, market outperformance, and field force expansion, while navigating moderate headwinds in Germany and US due to pricing pressure and regulatory delays; the Curatio acquisition strengthens its India portfolio and debt-funded growth strategy supports sustained momentum.
financial scorecard: rev:+7% YoY; EBITDA:29.4% (adjusted); PAT:unspecified; orderbook:unspecified; netdebt:+Rs.1,100-1,200cr net addition
guidance: India and Brazil to sustain double-digit growth; Germany to show modest improvement in Q4 driven by tender wins and new launches; US growth to remain pressured by price erosion; Curatio integration to contribute from Q3FY23 onwards; gross and EBITDA margins expected to remain stable in near term.
segment / subsidiary detail: India: Rs.1,224cr revenue (+13% YoY); 12 brands >Rs.100cr; 19% AIOCD growth (6% volume, 9% price, 4% new launches); Sitagliptin launched and ranked #1; trade generic at 2.5-3% contribution. Brazil: Rs.185cr revenue (+19% YoY; +10% CC); Rivaroxaban faced price erosion but market share rose to 4%; 7 new launches in 18 months; CNS field force expanded to 306 reps. Germany: Rs.220cr revenue (-12% YoY; -5% CC); 10 launches in H1; Q4 to see major impact from tender wins. US: Rs.292cr revenue (+3% YoY; +37M USD); 19 pending ANDAs; Form 483 received; price erosion at double-digit rate. Curatio: Acquired Oct 14, 2022; integration underway; funding via debt.
growth verticals / optionality: Curatio acquisition adds ~2 months of revenue in Q3FY23; potential for India inorganic growth via further acquisitions; Brazil pipeline offers multiple mid-size launch opportunities; Germany tender wins could accelerate growth; US approvals from Indrad plant (6-12 months post-FDA clearance) may provide incremental revenue.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin: 72% (improved sequentially); EBITDA: 29.4% (adjusted for Rs.7cr one-off); raw material costs stable overall; logistics costs remain elevated at Q3FY22 levels; no major cost increases expected in Q3.
capex / expansion: No major CAPEX planned for US; existing capacity utilization at 54%; sufficient for next 3 years; no new manufacturing investments announced; CAPEX focused on maintenance and organic scaling in India/Brazil.
capital allocation: Prioritizing inorganic growth in India (90-100% of Rs.100cr allocation over 5 years); Curatio funded via Rs.2,000cr debt (net debt increase of Rs.1,100-1,200cr after Rs.900cr repayment); debt cost ~7.2%; excess cash beyond growth opportunities to be returned as dividends.
risks & watch-items: US regulatory delays (Form 483 resolution pending); intense price erosion in US and Brazil (especially Rivaroxaban); Germany tender outcomes uncertain; Curatio integration risks; forex volatility (fully hedged 12-month forward); PLI scheme benefit insignificant until FY24.
management quality / tone: Confident and optimistic on India and Brazil growth; pragmatic on Germany and US challenges; transparent on regulatory issues and debt funding; focused on execution, market outperformance, and disciplined capital allocation; tone is steady, data-driven, and long-term oriented.
non-obvious takeaways: Torrent's market share leadership in key Indian brands (e.g., Gliclazide 70%, Nebivolol 47%) provides pricing power despite competition; Brazil's price regulation model (3-tier categories) allows strategic pricing flexibility; US portfolio is mature and deliberately de-prioritized in R&D/CAPEX, reducing burn while retaining revenue; Curatio’s contribution may be underappreciated as it’s not yet reflected in Q2 numbers.

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.
